STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple sits on a white plate. It is a snack, not a full meal.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The plate looks like a disposable paper side plate, about 22 cm across including the rim. Area = 3.14 × 11² ≈ 380 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: one whole red/yellow apple (Gala or Honeycrisp type), unpeeled.

STEP 4 - Area: The apple appears about 8.5 cm across, so its footprint is about 57 cm², or roughly 15% of the plate. Nothing else is on the plate, so total coverage is about 15%.

STEP 5 - Volume: A sphere is a poor fit for the footprint × height method, so I treat the apple as a spheroid about 8.5 cm wide and 7 cm tall. Volume ≈ 4/3 × π × 4.25² × 3.5 ≈ 265 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A whole apple has no air gaps, so I use a density of about 0.85 g/ml. 265 ml × 0.85 ≈ 225 g. Allowing for the core still being included, I settle on about 220 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple has about 52 kcal per 100 g, so 220 g × 0.52 ≈ 114 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A large apple typically weighs 200–250 g and has about 110–130 kcal, so the estimate is plausible.
